mechanisms.biological_system: Adult C. elegans AFD–AIY–RIM thermotaxis circuit

structural_evidence.summary: Adult connectome evidence supports named AFD/AIY/RIM cell classes and documented edges; a unique causal feedback carrier is not established.

functional_evidence.summary: Published class-level neural/behavior measures support the bounded source claim. Separate synthetic artificial abstractions have been tested; these are not biological endpoint reanalyses and do not establish transfer benefit.

mechanisms.identity_granularity: CELL_CLASS; exact left/right trace-to-neuron pairing is not established
mechanisms.result_scope: Biological E3 identifiability passed at cell-class granularity; E4 mechanism amendment remains externally underdetermined. Separate exploratory artificial abstractions were run: simple previous-action feedback helped only conditionally; synthetic state-gated gain was assumption-sensitive; the fixed gate lost to occupancy-matched/no-gate and memoryless controls in all 9 closed-loop test cells. An on-policy GRU beat the gate on the reused post-result suite. No AI-transfer benefit is established. A new post-result telegraph-target filtering study (M6) found the learned state gate beat a single global gain on the assumed high-reversal-noise profile, but lost to a two-parameter residual-adaptive filter at all three held-out hazards; equal-weighted gate-minus-adaptive MAE was +0.07587 (crossed 95% interval [+0.07314,+0.07864]). This synthetic reliability relation is not sourced from the worm experiments. A post-publication Figure 6C source-data reanalysis describes 1,008 WT and 3,910 RIM-ablated run events: event-weighted median duration 17.0 s vs 11.5 s, with lower RIM-ablated medians in all six coarse direction bins. The released event table has no worm IDs, so this is descriptive and supplies no new animal-level inference. A separate post-result corollary-discharge placement test found sensory-site feedback exceeded an equal-parameter output-persistence yoke by +0.06799 accuracy at hazard 0.05 (crossed 95% interval [+0.06475,+0.07120]) and shortened switch-recovery lag (1.30 vs 3.56 steps), but did not beat no feedback (88.94% vs 89.05%), a generic two-unit RNN (90.21%), or the Bayes reference (90.30%). This is a synthetic placement/stability tradeoff, not biological validation or an overall AI performance gain. A subsequent source-equation gradient-reversal stress test found the sensory-site feedback arm exceeded its no-feedback ablation in the translated model at all tested reversal schedules; at the 20-second schedule the paired progress difference was +0.07379 units/s (95% simulation seed-block interval [+0.07061,+0.07694], 100/100 positive). The direct output-site coefficient control saturated at 100% forward occupancy and 200-second runs, so it does not identify a feedback-site effect. This is model simulation only, not animal-level evidence or AI transfer. A further frozen-within-study synthetic transient-filter test (M2_SENSORIMOTOR_TRANSIENT_FILTER_V1) found output-site feedback better than sensory-site feedback on pulse-window MAE: output minus sensory = -0.0921, 95% paired seed-block bootstrap interval [-0.1081,-0.0766] across 20 blocks. No-feedback was worse than both placements, but this does not identify a biological computation or establish AI transfer; the result is exploratory and task-specific. A post-result paired secondary audit across all five synthetic conditions found lower mean movement MAE, higher command energy, and longer switch latency for output-site than sensory-site placement; movement-MSE ranking favored sensory-site placement in the two high-switch conditions. These are exploratory multi-comparison contrasts with no multiplicity correction, not a frozen multiobjective result.

Independent outcome-blind noise/reliability calibration or externally justified SESOI

Unique causal RIM-to-AIY synaptic carrier

The synthetic mode-dependent sensory-reliability relation was not established in the biological source
The artificial closed-loop gate is an abstract controller, not a reconstruction of the worm circuit
mechanisms.mechanism_definition: RIM-dependent state feedback modulates AIY activity and thermotactic motor-state representation at cell-class granularity, as bounded by the frozen biological evidence.
allowed_claim: AFD/AIY/RIM mechanism variables are identifiable at cell-class level under the completed E3 audit.
The public evidence is insufficient for the stronger E4 mechanism amendment.
The tested fixed artificial gate did not outperform the stated controls in the closed-loop benchmark; this does not refute the bounded biological findings.

In a synthetic telegraph-target estimation task with stipulated mode-dependent observation noise, a learned state gate beat a single global gain but lost to an equal-parameter residual-adaptive filter; this is an algorithmic result, not biological validation.

The released Figure 6C event table descriptively shows shorter RIM-ablated forward-run durations across six coarse direction bins; no animal-level inference is made because event-to-worm linkage is absent.

In a post-result synthetic telegraph-state task at hazard 0.05, feedback into a sensory-state update exceeded an equal-parameter output-persistence yoke by +0.06799 accuracy (crossed 95% interval [+0.06475,+0.07120]) and had shorter switch-recovery lag; it did not beat no feedback, a generic RNN, or a Bayes reference.

In a frozen-within-study synthetic binary tracking task, output-site feedback outperformed an equal-parameter sensory-site feedback model on transient-pulse movement MAE (output minus sensory -0.0921; 95% paired seed-block bootstrap interval [-0.1081,-0.0766]); no-feedback scored worse than both. This is task-specific artificial evidence, not biological validation.

In a post-result paired audit of five synthetic conditions, output-site feedback had lower mean absolute movement error, while using more command energy and taking longer to reacquire switches; squared-error ranking favored sensory-site feedback in high-switch conditions. These are exploratory secondary outcomes without multiplicity correction.

The underdetermined amendment is a biological FAIL.

mechanisms.artificial_abstraction: Three post-source abstractions were tested separately: previous-action persistence; motor-state-gated sensory gain; and a fixed state-gated controller in closed-loop target tracking. None is claimed to reproduce the biological circuit. M6 tests mode-specific sensory gain against residual-adaptive filtering on an independent telegraph-target estimation task; exploratory only. A separate three-parameter sensory-site feedback model was compared with an equal-parameter output-inertia yoke, a parameter-matched no-feedback ablation, a two-unit generic RNN, and a Bayes filter in a synthetic telegraph-state task; it showed a placement/switching effect only against the output yoke. A source-model stress test then simulated fixed versus sign-reversing warm gradients using the corrected Ji Figure 7 equations. The sensory-feedback arm exceeded no-feedback in simulated progress; an output-site coefficient control saturated and could not isolate site specificity. M2_SENSORIMOTOR_TRANSIENT_FILTER_V1 separately compared actual motor-state feedback in a scalar sensory update versus at the output under synthetic transient and sustained changes; output-site won the frozen pulse-window MAE contrast, and no-feedback was worse than both, with no biological validation.

mechanisms.biological_system: Mouse cerebellar circuit in delay eyeblink conditioning

source_publications.role: Optogenetic CF pairing sufficiency and CS-US timing dependence
CF/complex-spike sufficiency and timed inhibition necessity in delay eyeblink conditioning
Adjacent GrC/CF reward-interval timing source dataset; LTD weight profile is modeled in source analysis

structural_evidence.summary: The broad olivocerebellar CF-to-Purkinje pathway is established; the artificial model does not reconstruct biological wiring.

functional_evidence.summary: Primary experiments report CF/complex-spike responses and learned, appropriately timed eyelid responses under specified delay-conditioning protocols.

intervention_evidence.summary: Optogenetic CF stimulation substituted for sensory US; timed CF inhibition during airpuff US blocked learned conditioning while unconditioned reflex remained. Scope is delay eyeblink conditioning.

counterfactual_evidence.summary: Biological stimulation/inhibition contrasts exist. Artificial v3 is post-result exploratory and is not confirmatory.

mechanisms.identity_granularity: CELL_TYPE / CIRCUIT SIGNAL (climbing fiber and Purkinje complex-spike events); no single-synapse learning-rule claim
mechanisms.result_scope: A timed CF/complex-spike event causally instructs acquisition of an appropriately timed associative response in the tested delay eyeblink conditioning task. Eligibility trace and three-factor synaptic rule are computational abstractions, not directly measured algorithms. A fixed-hyperparameter follow-up retained a positive trace-versus-no-trace contrast across IID Gaussian, AR(1) Gaussian, and sparse-sign input streams (+0.2284 equal-generator accuracy; hierarchical task-seed 95% interval [+0.2213,+0.2357]; 30/30 positive task-seed averages in each generator). This keeps the same classification objective; exact replay remained superior in all 12 generator-delay cells. A post-result M7 sweep crossed six AR(1) correlations, four delays, and classification/regression objectives. Within each objective, the trace benefit generally decreased with rho at short delays but reversed at long delays; exact replay still beat the trace in all 48 cells. An initial pooled accuracy-minus-MSE interaction was invalid and is excluded. An adjacent Dryad reward-interval source-data analysis fit source-style CF-timed LTD projections within session and tested pre-reward GrC decoding of held-out reward delay. The CF-LTD projection did not beat the training-fold mean in 15/16 sessions and was worse on average in all three source groups; a raw-GrC PCA16 decoder showed only a small descriptive advantage in two expert groups. This is not the same task as the core delay-eyeblink intervention evidence and does not refute its causal result.
known_missing_evidence: Direct measurement and isolation of a particular synaptic eligibility-trace state/rule
Generalization to other cerebellum-dependent tasks and species
Artificial comparison against BPTT and broad modern online-learning algorithms
Independent post-result replication under a pre-outcome protocol
Timed CF-inhibition behavioral contrast used a modest cohort (four mice per condition) and CF opsin expression itself altered signaling in the source study.
mechanisms.mechanism_definition: Pairing of conditioned-stimulus-related activity with a temporally specific CF/complex-spike instructive event produces acquisition of a timed conditioned response in the tested task.
allowed_claim: The cited interventions support a causal CF/complex-spike instructive role in acquisition of mouse delay eyeblink conditioning.
A norm-matched local eligibility trace improved delayed-label accuracy over a no-trace misassignment control in the stated synthetic task.
With fixed hyperparameters, the synthetic trace effect remained positive versus no-trace across three tested input-stream distributions under the same task objective; exact replay remained superior.

On the fixed synthetic task family, trace benefit relative to current-input updates depends jointly on input autocorrelation, delay, and objective; objective-specific M7 interactions were positive when averaged over delay but reversed at long delays.

In an adjacent public reward-interval dataset, the tested source-style CF-LTD projection did not add held-out reward-delay predictive value beyond a within-session mean timer; generic raw-GrC decoding was small and group-dependent. This is an exploratory source-cohort result, not evidence against the distinct delay-eyeblink intervention findings.
